title: Geometrical terms
summary: Geometry questions expect the exact name for each angle, line, shape, solid and part of a circle, from [[quadrilateral|quadrilaterals]] to [[polygon|polygons]]. Learn the names and their facts, and naming questions become quick marks.

goals.text: Name angles by their size, and recognise [[parallel|parallel]] and [[perpendicular|perpendicular]] lines.
Tell [[congruent|congruent]] shapes from similar ones, and use a scale factor.
Name triangles, special quadrilaterals and polygons from their sides and angles.
Name simple solids, count their [[face|faces]], edges and vertices, and describe their nets.
Name the parts of a circle, such as a [[chord|chord]], a [[sector|sector]] and a [[segment|segment]].
Use the words [[plane|plane]], [[perpendicular-bisector|perpendicular bisector]], [[hemisphere|hemisphere]], [[frustum|frustum]], and major and minor [[arc|arc]].

before.prompt: A quarter turn is $90^{\circ}$. How many degrees are there in a full turn?
before.hint: A full turn is four quarter turns.

before.prompt: Two angles sit side by side on a straight line. One is $35^{\circ}$. Find the other, in degrees.
before.hint: Angles on a straight line add up to $180^{\circ}$.

blocks.text: A point marks a position. A line is straight and goes on for ever both ways. The part of a line between two points is a [[line-segment|line segment]].
A [[vertex|vertex]] (plural vertices) is a corner, where sides or edges meet.
[[parallel|Parallel]] lines stay the same distance apart, so they never meet. Diagrams mark them with matching arrows.
[[perpendicular|Perpendicular]] lines meet at a [[right-angle|right angle]], which is $90^{\circ}$. A small square in the corner marks a right angle.

blocks.alt: Four angles side by side. An acute angle of about 40 degrees, labelled less than 90 degrees. A right angle marked with a small square, labelled exactly 90 degrees. An obtuse angle of about 130 degrees, labelled 90 to 180 degrees. A reflex angle of about 235 degrees, with its arc going the long way round, labelled 180 to 360 degrees.
blocks.caption: Name an angle by comparing it with $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$.

blocks.text: An [[acute-angle|acute angle]] is less than $90^{\circ}$. An [[obtuse-angle|obtuse angle]] is between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$. A [[reflex-angle|reflex angle]] is between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$.
Two lines from one point, like $OP$ and $OQ$, make two angles that together make a full turn, $360^{\circ}$. Unless $OP$ and $OQ$ form a straight line, the larger one is reflex.

blocks.question: Lines $OP$ and $OQ$ meet at $O$. The smaller angle $POQ$ is $142^{\circ}$. Name its type, then find the reflex angle $POQ$.
steps: $142^{\circ}$ is between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$, so it is obtuse.
The two angles at $O$ make a full turn: reflex angle $POQ = 360^{\circ} - 142^{\circ} = 218^{\circ}$.
Check: $218^{\circ}$ is between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$, so it is reflex.

blocks.prompt: An angle measures $236^{\circ}$. Which type of angle is it?
blocks.explain: $236^{\circ}$ is between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$, so it is reflex.

blocks.text: The [[interior-angle|interior angle]] at a vertex of a shape is the angle inside it. Extend one side past the vertex: the angle between the extension and the next side is the [[exterior-angle|exterior angle]].

Where the interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$ (every vertex of a convex shape), the two angles make a straight line, so they sum to $180^{\circ}$. You will use them for polygons in {{lesson:4.6}}.

blocks.question: At one vertex of a shape, the interior angle is $107^{\circ}$. Find the exterior angle at that vertex.
steps: $107^{\circ}$ is less than $180^{\circ}$, so the interior and exterior angles sum to $180^{\circ}$.
Exterior angle $= 180^{\circ} - 107^{\circ} = 73^{\circ}$.

blocks.text: A [[bearing|bearing]] is a direction: an angle measured clockwise from north, written with three figures, such as $070^{\circ}$. More in {{lesson:4.3}}.

blocks.prompt: A boat sails due south-west. Which is its bearing?

blocks.text: The [[perpendicular-bisector|perpendicular bisector]] of $AB$ crosses $AB$ at right angles through its [[midpoint|midpoint]]. Every point on it is the same distance from $A$ as from $B$.

blocks.prompt: $P$ is on the perpendicular bisector of $AB$. $PA = (3x + 4)$ cm and $PB = (5x - 6)$ cm. Find $x$.

blocks.text: Calling an angle between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$ reflex. It is obtuse.

[[congruent|Congruent]] shapes are the same shape and size: one fits exactly on the other, even after turning or flipping. Matching sides and angles are equal. You won't need to prove shapes congruent.
[[similar-shapes|Similar]] shapes have the same shape but can differ in size. Matching angles are equal, and every length is multiplied by the same [[scale-factor|scale factor]].

blocks.tex: \text{scale factor} = \frac{\text{length on the new shape}}{\text{matching length on the original shape}}

blocks.question: Triangles $DEF$ and $KLM$ are congruent: $D$ matches $K$, $E$ matches $L$ and $F$ matches $M$. Angle $D = 52^{\circ}$ and angle $E = 71^{\circ}$. Find angle $M$.
steps: Angle $M$ matches angle $F$, so they are equal.
The [[angle-sum|angle sum]] of a triangle is $180^{\circ}$: angle $M = 180^{\circ} - 52^{\circ} - 71^{\circ} = 57^{\circ}$.

blocks.question: A photo $8$ cm wide and $5$ cm tall is enlarged to make a similar photo $20$ cm wide. Find the height of the enlarged photo.
steps: Scale factor $= \frac{20}{8} = 2.5$. It is more than $1$, as the photo got bigger.
Height $= 5 \times 2.5 = 12.5$ cm.

blocks.prompt: Rectangle $B$ is rectangle $A$ turned on its side. Which word fits best?
blocks.explain: Turning doesn't change size, so $A$ fits exactly on $B$: congruent.

blocks.prompt: A triangle has sides $3$ cm, $5$ cm and $6$ cm. A similar triangle has a shortest side of $12$ cm. Find its longest side, in cm.
blocks.hint: Use the two shortest sides for the scale factor.

blocks.text: Writing similar for shapes of the same size. Those are congruent.

An [[equilateral-triangle|equilateral triangle]] has three equal sides and three equal angles of $60^{\circ}$. An [[isosceles-triangle|isosceles triangle]] has two equal sides, and the two angles opposite them are equal.
A [[scalene-triangle|scalene triangle]] has no equal sides or angles. A [[right-angled-triangle|right-angled triangle]] has one angle of $90^{\circ}$.

blocks.question: An isosceles triangle has an angle of $46^{\circ}$ between its two equal sides. Find each of the other two angles.
steps: The other two angles are opposite the equal sides, so they are equal.
They share $180^{\circ} - 46^{\circ} = 134^{\circ}$, so each is $134^{\circ} \div 2 = 67^{\circ}$.

blocks.text: A [[quadrilateral|quadrilateral]] has four straight sides. Learn the special ones by their sides and angles.

blocks.alt: Six quadrilaterals with their names. Square: four equal sides and four right angles. Rectangle: four right angles, opposite sides equal. Parallelogram: two pairs of parallel sides, shown by single and double arrows. Rhombus: four equal sides, a diamond shape without right angles. Trapezium: one pair of parallel sides, top and bottom. Kite: two short equal sides at the top and two long equal sides at the bottom, each pair next to each other.
blocks.caption: Dashes mark equal sides. Arrows mark parallel sides.

blocks.text: Square: four equal sides and four right angles. Rectangle: four right angles, with opposite sides equal.
[[parallelogram|Parallelogram]]: two pairs of parallel sides, with opposite sides equal and opposite angles equal. [[rhombus|Rhombus]]: a parallelogram with four equal sides.
[[trapezium|Trapezium]]: one pair of parallel sides; the other two are not parallel. [[kite|Kite]]: two pairs of equal sides, each pair next to each other.
A square is also a rectangle and a rhombus. Give the name that fits every fact: four equal sides with no right angles is a rhombus.

blocks.prompt: A quadrilateral has exactly one pair of parallel sides. Name it.
blocks.hint: Count the pairs of parallel sides.
blocks.explain: One pair makes a trapezium. A parallelogram needs two.

blocks.prompt: Quadrilateral $ABCD$ has $AB = AD$ and $CB = CD$, but $AB \ne CB$. Name it.
blocks.hint: Are the equal sides opposite, or next to each other?
blocks.explain: Each pair of equal sides meets at a corner ($A$ and $C$), so it is a kite.

blocks.text: A [[polygon|polygon]] is a flat, closed shape with straight sides. A pentagon has $5$ sides, a hexagon $6$, an octagon $8$ and a decagon $10$.
A [[regular-polygon|regular polygon]] has all sides equal and all angles equal. Otherwise it is irregular.

blocks.question: A regular polygon has sides of $3.5$ cm and a perimeter of $35$ cm. Find its number of sides, $n$, and name the polygon.
steps: The sides are equal, so the perimeter is $n$ times one side: $n = 35 \div 3.5 = 10$.
$10$ sides makes it a regular decagon.

blocks.alt: A flat shape like a capital letter T, made of straight sides. A wide bar across the top sits on a narrower upright stem. Two of its corners, where the bar meets the stem, point inwards. Every corner is marked with a dot.

blocks.prompt: The shaded shape above has straight sides. Which polygon is it?
blocks.hint: Count every corner dot, including the inward ones.
blocks.explain: $8$ corners means $8$ sides: an irregular octagon.

blocks.text: Missing inward-pointing corners when counting sides. Dot every corner, then count.
A solid is a 3D shape. A [[face|face]] is a flat surface of it, an edge is where two faces meet, and a vertex is a corner.

blocks.alt: Six solids with their names, hidden edges dashed. Cube: six square faces. Triangular prism: the same triangle at each end, joined by three rectangles. Cylinder: two circular ends joined by a curved surface. Square-based pyramid: a square base with four triangular faces meeting at a point at the top. Cone: a circular base and a curved surface that rises to a point. Sphere: a round ball.
blocks.caption: Dashed lines are edges hidden at the back.

blocks.text: A cube has six square faces. A [[cuboid|cuboid]] is a box with six rectangular faces.

A [[prism|prism]] has flat faces and the same [[cross-section|cross-section]] all the way through and is named after it, such as a triangular prism. A [[cylinder|cylinder]] has two circular ends joined by a curved surface.
A [[pyramid|pyramid]] has a base and triangular faces meeting at a point. A [[cone|cone]] has a circular base and a curved surface rising to a point. A [[sphere|sphere]] is a ball.
A [[net|net]] is a flat shape that folds into a solid, with one part for each face.

blocks.question: A prism has a hexagon as its cross-section. Find its number of faces $F$, edges $E$ and vertices $V$.
steps: Faces: two hexagon ends and one rectangle per side, $F = 2 + 6 = 8$.
Edges: $6$ round each end and $6$ joining them, $E = 6 + 6 + 6 = 18$.
Vertices: $6$ at each end, $V = 2 \times 6 = 12$.

blocks.question: Find $F$, $E$ and $V$ for a square-based pyramid, and describe its net.
steps: Faces: the base and $4$ triangles, $F = 5$. Edges: $4$ round the base and $4$ to the top, $E = 8$.
Vertices: $4$ round the base and $1$ at the top, $V = 5$.
Its net is a square with a triangle on each side.

blocks.prompt: A solid has two flat circular faces joined by one curved surface. Name it.
blocks.hint: How many flat faces does a cone have?
blocks.explain: That is a cylinder. A cone has just one circle, plus a point.

blocks.prompt: How many edges does a triangular prism have?
blocks.hint: Count round each end, then the joining edges.

blocks.text: A [[plane|plane]] is a flat surface that goes on for ever. Each face of a cuboid lies in a plane. A [[hemisphere|hemisphere]] is half a sphere. A [[frustum|frustum]] is a cone or pyramid with its top cut off parallel to the base.

blocks.prompt: A square-based pyramid has its top cut off parallel to the base. How many faces does the frustum have?
blocks.hint: The cut makes a new face on top.

blocks.text: Every point on a circle is the same distance, the [[radius|radius]] (plural radii), from its centre.

blocks.alt: Two circles, each with centre O. Left circle: a diameter passes through O from one side of the circle to the other; a radius goes from O to the circle; a chord joins two points on the lower part of the circle without passing through O; a tangent line touches the circle at one point on the lower right; the curve itself is labelled circumference. Right circle: a shaded sector between two radii and the arc joining them, at the top right; a shaded segment between a chord and the arc below it, at the bottom; and a short arc on the left, drawn as a thick part of the curve.

blocks.text: A [[chord|chord]] joins two points on the circle. A [[diameter|diameter]] is a chord through the centre, twice the radius.
The [[circumference|circumference]] is the whole way round. An [[arc|arc]] is part of it. A [[tangent|tangent]] is a straight line touching the circle at one point only.

A [[sector|sector]] is the slice between two radii and an arc. A [[segment|segment]] is the part cut off by a chord, between the chord and its arc. A diameter splits the circle into two [[semicircle|semicircles]].

blocks.question: A round table top has a diameter of $1.3$ m. Find its radius.
steps: A diameter is two radii end to end, so radius $= 1.3 \div 2 = 0.65$ m.

blocks.question: $A$ and $B$ lie on a circle with centre $O$. Angle $AOB = 64^{\circ}$. Find angle $OAB$.
steps: $OA$ and $OB$ are radii, so $OA = OB$ and triangle $OAB$ is isosceles.
Angle $OAB = (180^{\circ} - 64^{\circ}) \div 2 = 58^{\circ}$.

blocks.prompt: Which part of a circle is the region between two radii and an arc?
blocks.explain: Two radii cut off a sector. A chord cuts off a segment.

blocks.prompt: A straight line meets a circle at exactly one point. Name the line.
blocks.hint: A chord meets the circle twice.
blocks.explain: Touching at one point only makes it a tangent.

blocks.text: Two points on a circle split it into two arcs. Unless the points are the ends of a diameter, the shorter is the minor arc and the longer is the major arc. Sectors and segments are minor or major in the same way.

blocks.prompt: Minor arc $PQ$ makes $128^{\circ}$ at the centre $O$. Find the angle at $O$ for the major arc $PQ$, in degrees.
blocks.hint: The two arcs make the whole circle.

blocks.text: Calling every chord a diameter. Only a chord through the centre is one.
Acute $< 90^{\circ}$; right $= 90^{\circ}$; obtuse between $90^{\circ}$ and $180^{\circ}$; reflex between $180^{\circ}$ and $360^{\circ}$.
At a vertex where the interior angle is less than $180^{\circ}$, interior angle $+$ exterior angle $= 180^{\circ}$.
Congruent: same shape and size. Similar: same shape, lengths times the scale factor.
Parallelogram: two pairs of parallel sides. Trapezium: one pair. Rhombus: four equal sides. Kite: two pairs of equal neighbouring sides.
Pentagon $5$, hexagon $6$, octagon $8$, decagon $10$ sides.
Diameter $= 2 \times$ radius, through the centre.
Sector: between two radii and an arc. Segment: between a chord and an arc.
Minor and major arc angles at the centre add up to $360^{\circ}$.

mistakes: Calling a shape with one pair of parallel sides a parallelogram. That is a trapezium.
Mixing up sector and segment. Two radii make a sector; a chord makes a segment.
Calling four equal sides with no right angles a square. It is a rhombus.
Calling a solid with one circular face and a point a cylinder. It is a cone.
examTips: To write down a name, give the exact mathematical word with no working, spelled clearly (isosceles, trapezium).
Use every fact given. Four equal sides could be a square or a rhombus; no right angles decides it.
Don't measure a diagram marked not to scale. Read its marks: dashes for equal sides, arrows for parallel sides, a square for $90^{\circ}$.
